title: The Prayer of a Forgiven Man

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelek, his wife and his female slaves so they could have children again, for the Lord had closed all the wombs in Abimelek's household because of Abraham's wife Sarah. - Gen 20:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with Abraham praying, and God healing. Abimelech's household had been struck with barrenness because of what happened with Sarah; now Abraham intercedes, and God restores fruitfulness to them. The failed, forgiven man becomes the channel of blessing to the very household he had endangered.

There is a beautiful completeness to this. Abraham fell, was rebuked, was restored - and now he is praying effectively for others, and God is answering. The one whose sin brought trouble on this household becomes, by grace, the one whose prayer brings healing to it. God restores His fallen servant fully, back into fruitful ministry to others.

Notice the irony and the grace together. Abraham, who could not yet have his own promised child, prays for barren wombs to be opened - and God does it. The man still waiting on his own promise becomes the means of blessing for others. God's grace flows through us to others even while we ourselves are still waiting.

This is how God loves to work. He takes forgiven failures and makes them intercessors. He takes people who have caused harm and, through repentance and restoration, makes them a blessing. Your failures, brought to God, need not be the end of your usefulness. Like Abraham, you can be restored and become a channel of God's healing to others. "The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective" (Jas 5:16) - even the prayer of one recently restored.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God can make you a blessing to others even after failure?
- Who might God be calling you to pray for and bless today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You restore forgiven failures and make them intercessors. Take my brokenness and make me a channel of Your blessing to others. Let my prayers, though imperfect, bring healing by Your grace.
Amen.
